headline: High: ctx can observe Claude Code events and use filesystem/MCP surfaces, creating default-path prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks when paired with Chatwoot's customer-support workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot ingests customer messages and integrations, while ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events and MCP activity. That creates a plausible path where content from Chatwoot is forwarded into ctx-managed workflows and then treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is copied into Claude Code or an MCP-backed workflow that ctx observes, injection becomes reachable.
IF ctx parses observed tool output as actionable instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding of Chatwoot text into Claude Code workflows.
Add a strict allowlist for ctx-observed events and ignore free-form message bodies.
Require human review before any instruction extracted from customer content is acted on.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags so ctx can distinguish data from instructions.
requires-engineering: isolate Chatwoot and ctx into separate workspaces with no shared clipboard or queue.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, orders, messages, and reports; ctx touches agent entities, harness records, graph data, and audit/runtime logs, and can access filesystem plus GitHub/Claude Code. A shared workspace or log path could expose sensitive support data to ctx and then onward through its APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports tickets or reports into a filesystem path ctx watches, leakage is reachable.
IF ctx uploads observed files or logs to GitHub/Claude Code, sensitive support data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Store Chatwoot exports in a directory ctx cannot read.
Redact customer identifiers before any file is handed to ctx.
Turn off verbose runtime logging for shared workflows.
requires-engineering: separate credentials and workspaces for Chatwoot and ctx.
requires-engineering: block ctx from reading support-data directories with OS permissions.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and integrations, while ctx can install packages, run browsers, and supports multiple instances with filesystem access. Even without explicit write scopes listed, overlapping mutable surfaces and concurrent instances create a realistic conflict path on shared files or automation state. Because the exact shared resource is not documented, uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or config directory, state races become reachable.
IF ctx runs multiple instances against Chatwoot-managed artifacts, concurrent modification conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories to each agent.
Pause one agent before the other mutates shared artifacts.
Use file locks for any shared export or sync path.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared resources.
requires-engineering: restrict browser/package actions to a sandboxed temp directory.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces customer-support outputs and ctx is explicitly a harness that observes tool events and can act through Claude Code, GitHub, and browsers. If ctx treats Chatwoot-generated text or summaries as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits, automation, or external actions. The downstream action surface is documented for ctx, so the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is fed into ctx without verification, ctx may propagate incorrect facts.
IF ctx uses that output to drive GitHub, browser, or Claude Code actions, the error can become externally visible.
mitigations: Require a verification step before ctx acts on Chatwoot output.
Mark Chatwoot-derived text as untrusted in downstream prompts.
Limit ctx to read-only observation for support workflows.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for any Chatwoot-to-ctx handoff.
requires-engineering: gate external actions behind human approval.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data, contact profiles, orders, messages, and reports, while ctx stores audit/runtime logs and graph data and can interact with GitHub/Claude Code. If customer-support data is routed into ctx logs or repositories, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions or certifications, so the risk is compliance mismatch rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF customer-support records are copied into ctx audit/runtime logs, retention policy mismatch becomes reachable.
IF support data is pushed to GitHub through ctx, residency and access-control obligations may change.
mitigations: Do not place customer records in ctx logs or repositories.
Set a short log-retention window for any shared workflow.
Review whether support data may leave the original system before enabling sync.
requires-engineering: document data-flow and residency boundaries.
requires-engineering: add deletion/export handling for any copied support data.
